profile_notes: The dominant search intent for an astro lens is wide-field nightscape / Milky Way work, and the sources converge tightly on two hard requirements plus a distinctive optical signature. HARD GATES: focal_length_mm <= 35 and max_aperture <= 2.8 (remember max_aperture is an f-number, lower = faster). Rationale for the numbers: sources place the nightscape sweet spot at 14-24mm with the 20-24mm range especially prized, and effectively no wide-field astro recommendation exceeds 35mm; a 35mm ceiling captures 14/20/24/28/35 primes and the classic ultra-wide zooms (14-24, 16-35) while excluding standard/portrait/tele glass. f/2.8 is the universally-cited workhorse threshold (primes at f/1.4-f/2 are better still but f/2.8 is the accepted floor for gathering enough starlight at manageable exposure times), so <= 2.8 is a reliable, well-populated gate. WEIGHTS: coma (3) is THE classic astro criterion -- off-axis stars smearing into wings/seagulls when a fast lens is shot wide open -- and is co-top. optical_performance (3) carries edge-to-edge sharpness on point sources. vignetting (2) is heavily corrected in fast wides and light falloff at the corners lifts noise when brightened. chromatic_aberration (2) shows as color fringing on bright stars. distortion (1), color_rendition (1) for star color, filter_thread (1) for light-pollution filters, build (1) for cold/dew, handling (1) for a usable manual-focus ring at infinity -- all mild. Axes OMITTED (weight 0): af_performance and af_noise (astro focuses manually at infinity) and bokeh (irrelevant to point-source star fields). CAVEATS for Lee: (1) The focal_length_mm gate assumes zooms are populated by their WIDE end; if a 24-70/2.8 or 24-105 is stored with a min focal of 24 it will pass both gates -- mild, defensible over-inclusion since the wide end is usable for Milky Way, but flagging it. (2) A 35mm/f2.8 ceiling deliberately excludes the deep-sky telephoto sub-genre (e.g. 135mm f/1.8 for nebulae); that is a separate, smaller use case -- confirm you want this guide scoped to nightscape/wide-field only. (3) If we later want to reward the truly fast primes, consider tightening to <= 2.0, but that would drop the many capable f/2.8 ultra-wide zooms, so left at 2.8. Research basis: astrobackyard, capturetheatlas, photopills, slrlounge on focal-length/aperture/coma. Ratified by Lee 2026-09-14
